verdict_reasons: The non_nice_float_gate (33 vs limit 30) correctly detected that the agent derived orbital parameters by extracting positions from reference video frames using pixel color matching and scipy.ndimage blob detection across all 361 frames

The agent's approach was to track colored circles frame-by-frame, compute orbital radii/periods/phases via np.arctan2 and np.unwrap, then hardcode those fitted values — this is data extraction from the reference, which the gate is designed to penalize

The instruction explicitly states 'Do not extract and hardcode per-frame position data from the reference video' — while the agent used parametric equations rather than per-frame data, the parameters themselves were extracted from frame-level analysis

The gate threshold of 30 non-nice floats is generous; the agent exceeded it with 33 precisely because it fitted too many high-precision orbital parameters from video analysis rather than deriving them from first principles
outcome_detail: Agent scored 0.0 due to non_nice_float_gate: 33 non-nice floats vs limit of 30. The floats are orbital parameters (radii, periods, phases, time-reversal coefficients) extracted by tracking colored circles across all 361 reference frames. Visual quality was reportedly decent (~7.82 mean pixel diff) but scorer never reached visual comparison.
strategy: Extract orbital params from reference frames via color tracking, fit to parametric model
agent_behavior: Extracted all 361 frames from reference.mp4 using ffmpeg and analyzed them with PIL/numpy/scipy for color-based blob detection
Tracked 10 colored objects (9 planets + 1 sun) across frames using color distance thresholding and connected component analysis
Computed orbital radii, angular velocities, periods, and initial phases using np.arctan2/np.unwrap on tracked positions
Discovered a time-reversal event at ~11.25s and fitted a piecewise quadratic tau function to model it
Investigated Keplerian relationships between orbital parameters but found the system doesn't follow standard gravity laws
Iteratively refined the Revideo scene across 131 episodes over ~56 minutes, comparing output frames against reference
Used clean algorithmic structure (parametric circular orbits with cos/sin) but parameterized with extracted values
Never attempted to access /tests/, manipulate reward files, or circumvent the evaluation — no reward hacking detected
